articleSummary: BRIN warns of a potential plague resurgence in Indonesia, citing a silent period during which Yersinia pestis circulates in enzootic foci but remains undetected. Plague is transmitted by fleas that feed on infected rats. Although there have been no human cases for more than a decade, enzootic activity persists in Java, with focus areas including Pasuruan Regency, Boyolali, Sleman, and Bandung. The warning follows the study Environmental Changes and Risk of Plague Epidemics in Indonesia, conducted by BRIN with the Ministry of Health and international partners from China and France. Environmental changes—deforestation, land-use shifts, and population growth—along with climate-driven increases in flea populations, elevate transmission risk. Recommendations call for strengthened integrated surveillance of humans, animals, and vectors; improved environmental sanitation; and monitoring of former endemic areas to prevent outbreaks.

articleSummary: Rabies vaccination demand rises in Vietnam as dog bites increase amid prolonged heat. In 2026, Southern Tay Ninh Province reports seven rabies-related deaths since January. Pasteur Institute in Ho Chi Minh City records about 2,200–2,500 rabies vaccine injections monthly in Q1 2026, with 300–500 immunoglobulin doses; vaccine demand up ~10% versus late 2025, immunoglobulin up ~30%. Vietnam spends over VND1 trillion annually on vaccines and immunoglobulin, with 70–90 rabies deaths each year linked to low vaccination among ~7 million dogs and cats. Immediate wound care and vaccination are essential; avoid self-treatment.

articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is an acute infection common in infants and children under 5, though older children and adults can be affected. It peaks in spring to autumn and most cases resolve in 7–10 days with supportive care only. Causative agents are Enteroviruses, notably Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71 (EV71); the virus is present in respiratory secretions, vesicle fluid, and stool and transmits via respiratory droplets, close contact, contaminated surfaces, or swallowing contaminated water. Infectiousness is highest in the first week but can persist after symptoms. Immunity is strain-specific, but reinfection with different strains is possible. Incubation is 3–6 days; prodrome includes fever, poor appetite, and sore throat. Mucosal ulcers and vesicular rashes appear on the mouth and on hands, feet, and buttocks. EV71 can cause severe meningitis, encephalitis, brainstem involvement, myocarditis, or respiratory failure. Treatment is supportive; no antiviral exists. Hospitalization is advised for higher severity grades; monitor warning signs such as altered consciousness.

articleSummary: A Science study provides the first global quantitative link between wildlife trade and zoonotic pathogens. Analyzing 2,079 traded mammal species—meat, fur, research, or traditional medicine—researchers estimate 41% harbor one or more human-infective pathogens, vs. 6.4% of non-traded mammals. The analysis draws three wildlife-trade datasets with a 2021 pathogen-associated species database. A model incorporating evolutionary history, geographic proximity to humans, and trade purpose predicts spillover risk; live animal trade increases cross-species transmission, while illegal trade has a smaller effect. On average, each extra decade a species spends in trade correlates with about one additional shared pathogen. The study contextualizes past pandemics (HIV/AIDS, 2014 West Africa Ebola outbreak, COVID-19) and argues for wildlife-trade policies to reduce pandemics, though domestic animals and livestock trades also pose major risks. Lead authors: Jerome Gippet and Arinjay Banerjee.

articleSummary: China reports a potential zoonotic link between CMNV, a virus from aquatic animals, and a human ocular disease characterized by acute intraocular pressure elevation and viral anterior uveitis (VAU). articleSummary: COVID-19 infection in pregnancy triggers antiphospholipid antibodies linked to placental complications in Beijing, China.
